name: Leveraged perpetual longs
constraint_note: Closed out by the venue's maintenance margin rule, automatically, so the order arrives whatever the price is.
evidence: Venue margin documentation, and the measured tape carries the resulting moves.
falsifier: Liquidation is discretionary, or owners close gradually before the rule bites.

name: Passive index funds and tracking vehicles
constraint_note: They must hold the index as defined, so an addition is a purchase at any price on the effective date and a deletion is a sale.
evidence: Published index methodology and the funds' registration statements; holdings are filed quarterly.
falsifier: Funds may transition over a window wide enough to trade at market prices instead.

name: Option dealers and market makers
constraint_note: A written option leaves them short gamma, so they must buy into strength and sell into weakness, until their risk limits stop them.
evidence: Dealer positioning literature, and the observable link between open interest and realised volatility.
falsifier: They warehouse the risk through the event, or offset it inside their own book.

name: Fixed price engineering and construction contractors
constraint_note: A fixed price obligation makes a schedule slip cost them money they cannot bill, so they absorb the shock and eventually renegotiate.
evidence: Quanta reports roughly 56 percent of revenue as fixed price in its own segment revenue facts; unapproved change orders are disclosed in XBRL.
falsifier: Contracts pass schedule cost through to the owner.

name: Project lenders and completion covenant holders
constraint_note: Credit is released against milestones, so a revision changes when money moves and can force a waiver, a repricing or a drawdown.
evidence: Project finance agreements appear in exhibits; the obligation panel measures publication timing.
falsifier: Facilities carry wide schedule latitude.

name: Interconnection queue operator and its rules
constraint_note: Who energises and when is decided by a first come, first served queue with study milestones, so a position decides whether a project is built at all.
evidence: Published queue procedures, and 274,176 MW of promised capacity that moved; the queue itself is not reachable from this host.
falsifier: Queue position does not predict energisation once size and technology are held.

name: Compute capacity providers and lessors
constraint_note: Deployed inventory cannot be reallocated quickly, so they price against their own occupancy rather than against a clearing market.
evidence: Ten families with a median pairwise daily correlation of minus 0.01; the archive is provider listed pricing.
falsifier: Rental capacity is fungible across families, so one price emerges and the dispersion is a listing artefact.

name: Hyperscaler and data centre buyers of equipment
constraint_note: They commit capex against a delivery date, so a supplier slip pushes their buildout and forces a substitution purchase or a penalty.
evidence: Remaining performance obligations and capex commitments are reported and measured; the median disclosure lag is 56 days.
falsifier: Commitments are soft, so a slip is absorbed without substitution.

name: Data centre landlords and their tenants
constraint_note: Leases run for years with escalation, so the landlord collects on a schedule while the tenant carries the cost of delay.
evidence: Segment revenue shows rental lines at 99 percent of revenue for one large landlord and about half for one small host.
falsifier: Rents are tied to availability, so delay risk stays with the landlord.

name: Equipment suppliers: turbines, transformers, switchgear, servers
constraint_note: Capacity is fixed in the short run, so an order surge becomes a lead time and a price rather than a volume.
evidence: Measured lead time share from contracted backlog; supplier segment revenue shows the diversification.
falsifier: Capacity expands fast enough that orders become volume rather than price.

direction: out of a leveraged long, into whoever absorbs it
size_note: within ten basis points, 3.3m per side on one large crypto perpetual and 8.6m on the second
data_note: Forward tape of book, funding and open interest from the public API; the historical archive path is not found.
evidence: Pre-registered trigger rule and a running collector; 455 samples per market with no trigger yet.
falsifier: After costs, post trigger reversion is absent once the trigger is conditioned on.

direction: into an added constituent and out of a deleted one, on the effective date
calendar: announced ahead, executed at a fixed close
size_note: not yet measured; scales with tracked assets
data_note: Provider announcements are published; fund holdings are filed quarterly.
evidence: Published methodology and the existence of the tracking vehicles.
falsifier: The forced trade is fully anticipated, so the effective date shows no flow.

direction: with the move when short gamma, against it when long
size_note: not measured; needs a surface and open interest
data_note: Historical option chains are the missing dataset, so an entitlement is needed.
evidence: Established in the literature, not measured here.
falsifier: Hedging flow has no effect on the underlying beyond its own movement.

direction: from the contractor's margin to whoever supplies recovery
calendar: monthly and quarterly, as work is certified
size_note: 3,783 promises moved with a modal annual revision of twelve months
data_note: Contract exhibits and XBRL facts are reachable; the missing capability is joining a project to the firm that bears its schedule risk.
evidence: The survival panel and the hazard rising with age, plus the disclosed fixed price share.
falsifier: No firm level sensitivity to its own project revisions once sector and size are controlled.

direction: from committed capital to the project, on milestones
data_note: Facility agreements in exhibits; borrowings partly visible in quarterly filings.
evidence: The obligation panel measures publication timing, 56 days median.
falsifier: Facilities carry wide schedule latitude.

mechanism: first come, first served study process
direction: from late projects to early ones as the queue clears
size_note: 274,176 MW moved across 1,070 entities, only 6.2 percent with a large listed owner
data_note: Operator files are published but unreachable from this host; the request is written.
evidence: The measured slippage distribution and the attribution ceiling.
falsifier: Queue position has no relation to energisation timing once technology and size are held.

direction: from the buyer to the provider when a family is scarce
size_note: ten families, dispersion measured, p5 near seventy dollars per instance hour against p4d at eleven
data_note: Provider listed pricing is reachable; executed rentals are not, and no issuer reports a family split.
evidence: The family correlation matrix and the issuer segment probe.
falsifier: One price emerges across families, or a listed issuer isolates one family.

direction: from the slotted supplier to whoever can deliver sooner
data_note: Capex commitments and obligations are reported; the 8-K coverage we hold is four firms.
evidence: Reported capex commitments and the measured disclosure lag.
falsifier: Deliveries do not substitute, so a slip delays the buildout instead.

size_note: 99 percent of one large landlord's revenue is rental
data_note: Lease terms and segment revenue are in the annual report, already reachable.
evidence: The segment revenue probe.
falsifier: Rents are indexed to availability.

direction: from buyers to suppliers, as lead time and price
size_note: lead time share and backlog growth measured monthly
data_note: Contracted backlog is reported and measured; the delivery times survey is reachable.
evidence: The measured lead time factors, which moved price and not delivery in our tests.
falsifier: Capacity expands fast enough that the surge becomes volume rather than price.

description: Equity of a data centre landlord

evidence: The instrument is the object the forced flow clears in, and capacity was measured from the book.
falsifier: Reversion after a trigger disappears once costs and capacity are applied.

evidence: Median 56 day lag from period end to public availability, from acceptance timestamps.
falsifier: The disclosure is not read, so the lag carries no price effect.

evidence: The queue decides energisation, and the attribution ceiling limits the equity expression.
falsifier: Queue position does not predict energisation once size and technology are held.

evidence: Family dispersion measured, and no issuer reports a family split.
falsifier: A listed issuer isolates a family and shows no sensitivity to its scarcity.

evidence: Capex commitments are reported and measured with their disclosure lag.
falsifier: A slip in the user's plan does not move the supplier's order book.

evidence: Hourly generation by balancing authority is measured, and energisation is what changes it.
falsifier: Energisation timing does not appear in the balancing authority series.

evidence: The quantity is defined by the index rule and the assets that track it, and both are public.
falsifier: The effective date shows no flow once the announcement is controlled for.

evidence: Dealer hedging is the mechanism that converts open interest into underlying demand.
falsifier: Hedging demand has no measurable relation to the underlying return around a known event.

evidence: Milestone certification is what releases the capital, and the obligation disclosures time it.
falsifier: Drawdown timing shows no relation to the schedule revisions we measure.

evidence: Rental lines are 99 percent of one large landlord's revenue and about half of one host's.
falsifier: The lease rate shows no relation to compute scarcity or to availability.

evidence: Lead time share and backlog growth are measured monthly from reported backlog.
falsifier: Lead time share has no relation to supplier pricing or to delivery.
